title: Hamamyolu Urban Deck
description: Spanning 26,088 m² in the former centre of Eskişehir, the intervention reinvents the pedestrian axis of Hamamyolu Street, reconnecting the city’s north and south, creating a continuous pedestrian route of 1.2 km embedded with a glass-and-LED line (22,000 local handmade glass pieces), planting 50 new lindens plus 3,877 ivies and 2,622 shrubs to form a green belt, and transforming the street into a vibrant public space that supports both tourism and daily life
physical_innovation: The project replaces a vehicle-dominated axis with a layered structure: surfaces are over-decked (‘urban deck’), a pedestrian bridge passes over the former road, a continuous LED and handmade glass inlay marks the path, existing and new trees create a green corridor, and integrated play and water elements are embedded into the deck, thereby merging infrastructure, culture, green and blue systems
social_innovation: By reconnecting north and south parts of the city via a pedestrian axis and creating a highly useable public zone with cafés, amphitheatres, playgrounds and seating (free seating capacity increased from 1,000 to 5,000) the project transformed the space into a social magnet that supports cultural identity, craft economy (glass production), community gathering and inter-age usage.
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.
c5_impacts:
Pedestrian connectivity
The project transformed 26,088 m² of road-dominated public space into a continuous pedestrian axis over 1.2 km, reconnecting previously fragmented areas of Eskişehir’s historic centre and revitalising commercial and cultural activities along the route.
Microclimate
Three pools — the Stone Pool, Steam Pool, and Pigeon Pool — introduce evaporative cooling and enhance the sensory quality of the public realm, mitigating the heat stress
Social inclusion and accessibility
The new pedestrian deck increased seating capacity from ~1,000 to 5,000 people, enabling multigenerational use, open-air cultural events, and accessible leisure for children, elderly, and visitors
Urban safety and liveability
Conversion from vehicular traffic to pedestrian use reduced traffic hazards and noise, enhancing perceived and actual safety.

title: Ballerup Boulevard
description: The boulevard was transformed from a four-lane high-traffic road into a two-lane green boulevard. The former road surface was narrowed and repurposed into green planting beds, tree avenues, storm-water infiltration areas and wide pedestrian/cycle paths, thus converting a barrier into a connective, human-scale green corridor.
physical_innovation: The project physically retreated the vehicular footprint by reducing from four to two lanes, and established extensive planting beds, tree groves and storm-water infiltration strips along the sidewalks and cycle tracks.
social_innovation: By shifting the emphasis from cars to people and green space, the boulevard now offers wide pedestrian and cycle zones, informal recreation areas, and a more favourable environment for social interaction and neighbourhood connectivity.
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.

Social and environmental benefit
Improved air quality, noise reduction, and higher social use of public realm recorded post-completion
Storm-water management
Infiltration trenches and permeable surfaces handle runoff locally, reducing sewer load.
Reduction of vehicular area
Road lanes reduced from four to two, cutting paved surface by approximately 50 %.

title: Little C
designer: CULD (Juurlink + Geluk, in collaboration with INBO Architects and Office Winhov)
description: Little C transforms a neglected infrastructural void between highways and canals near Coolhaven into a vibrant mixed-use neighbourhood of 15 compact blocks. Combining brick architecture, pedestrian bridges, lush courtyards, green façades, and roof gardens, the project reconnects fragmented urban fabrics, introduces sustainable water management, and creates new public and semi-public spaces.
physical_innovation: The project overlays dense urban form with multilayered green infrastructure: green roofs, vertical planting, water-retention decks beneath pavements, and new micro-courtyards create a resilient “city within the city.” It merges architectural density with permeability and ecosystem functions.
social_innovation: Little C fosters social connection through shared gardens, semi-public courtyards, pedestrian bridges, and communal roof terraces. The design enables encounters and inclusion within a high-density context, redefining liveability in compact urban quarters.

title: Girondins Development Area (ZAC des Girondins)
designer: BASE Landscape Architecture, with EGIS VRD, Transitec, Les Éclaireurs
promoter: SERL – Société d’Équipement du Rhône et de Lyon
description: The area is a 17.5 ha urban regeneration project in Lyon’s Gerland district. The masterplan transforms an industrial site into a mixed-use neighbourhood structured by 2 axes: the Allée Fontenay (N-S green boulevard) and Rue des Girondins (E-W avenue). The design integrates green-blue infrastructure, sustainable drainage systems (SUDS), and inclusive public spaces, turning the site into a climate-resilient, vibrant quarter. The project demonstrates systemic integration of urban morphology, ecological infrastructure, and climate adaptation. The “green and blue backbone” operates as a multifunctional spine—both a hydrological system and a bioclimatic corridor.
physical_innovation: The project transforms a former industrial brownfield into a porous and climate-responsive urban fabric. A continuous green-blue infrastructure — including rain gardens, vegetated swales, permeable paving, and tree-lined boulevards — manages stormwater, reduces heat, and enhances biodiversity. The Allée Fontenay acts as a linear climatic corridor, integrating mobility, shade, and ecological continuity within the dense urban grid. Landscape and infrastructure merge into a multifunctional system that turns the public realm into an adaptive device for climate resilience.
social_innovation: The masterplan promotes social inclusion and everyday interaction through accessible, shaded public spaces and shared courtyards. The layout encourages proximity, community life, and mixed uses along green pedestrian routes. Co-design activities and public consultations coordinated by SERL involved citizens and local associations in defining uses and management, strengthening civic ownership and social cohesion.
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.
c5_impacts:
Ecological connectivity
The Allée Fontenay creates a continuous 1 km green corridor linking Gerland’s fragmented ecological systems.
Surface permeability and stormwater management
Permeable and vegetated areas increased by more than 40 % compared to pre-development. SUDS and vegetated ditches reduce runoff and flooding risk.
Biodiversity
Hundreds of trees and native species introduced, providing new habitats for urban fauna.
Thermal comfort improvement
Shaded and ventilated corridors mitigate heat stress during summer peaks
Social inclusion
Public spaces promote interaction and accessibility for all age groups.

title: Freiburger Bächle
year: Origin 12th–13th century; restored and enhanced over time (most recent 19th–21st century)
description: The Bächle are narrow open-water channels running along the streets of Freiburg's old town. Fed by the Dreisam River, they form a continuous blue infrastructure originally used for irrigation, firefighting and drainage. Today they serve as a cultural symbol, micro-climatic cooling system and playful urban amenity, fostering social interaction and comfort in the historic centre.
physical_innovation: Reactivation of an historical open-water network as urban cooling infrastructure. The Bächle channel fresh river water through the city centre, improving microclimate, reducing urban heat and enhancing sensory quality. Their continuous, low-depth design integrates seamlessly with narrow medieval streets.
social_innovation: The Bächle act as informal social infrastructure: children play with water, residents and tourists interact along the canals, and the channels strengthen place identity. Their accessibility and symbolic value support community life and cultural heritage.
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.
c5_impacts:
Urban cooling and pedestrian comfort
The flowing water creates evaporative cooling, reducing perceived temperature during summer peaks. Bächle improve the sensory experience of streets and attract foot traffic, supporting local commerce.

Public space activation
Children and families use Bächle as playful micro-places, enhancing vibrancy and dwell time in the historic centre.

Cultural identity reinforcement
he canals strengthen local identity and heritage, contributing to Freiburg’s branding and tourism appeal.

Blue infrastructure resilience
Water circulation from the Dreisam provides continuous flushing and supports runoff management.

title: Calle María Díaz de Haro – Climate-Adapted Green Corridor
designer: Bilbao City / Municipal Urban Planning Department
description: Transformation of a 700 m traffic-dominated street into a green and permeable pedestrian-oriented corridor. The project reduces car lanes, removes parking, widens sidewalks, adds trees and planting strips, and integrates permeable surfaces to mitigate heat and manage stormwater. It creates a distributed climatic refuge and improves ecological continuity between Casilda Park and Ametzola.
physical_innovation: Conversion of a three-lane road into a permeable, shaded green corridor. Two traffic lanes and parking are replaced by wide sidewalks, planting beds, and continuous tree rows. Permeable pavements and vegetated strips control runoff and mitigate urban heat. The works redesigned over 4,500 m² of pedestrian space with permeable surfaces, improved infiltration, and lowered surface temperatures. A continuous corridor of deciduous, perennial, native species enhances shade, evapotranspiration cooling, and ecological continuity. The intervention also added 1,300 m² of retention areas and removed more than 2,800 m² of asphalt.
social_innovation: The corridor becomes a comfortable public space supporting walkability, rest areas, social interaction, and everyday outdoor life. It strengthens pedestrian connections between key neighbourhood facilities and parks.
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.

Increase in permeable pedestrian surface
The transformation of the street created over 4,500 m² of new pedestrian areas built with permeable materials. This expansion reduces surface temperatures, supports natural infiltration, and improves the thermal comfort of daily walking routes.
Stormwater retention capacity added
Through the introduction of rain gardens, green strips, and bioretentive soil sections, the project integrated approximately 1,300 m² of stormwater retention zones, significantly improving local flood resilience during heavy rainfall events.
Reduction of impermeable road surface and traffic volumes
By removing more than 2,800 m² of asphalt roadway, the project decreased car lanes and eliminated parking areas, resulting in a measurable reduction in vehicular traffic volumes, lower emissions, and improved air quality along the corridor.

title: Zollhallen Plaza
description: A 5,600 m² post-industrial plaza adjacent to the historic customs hall, redesigned with water-sensitive urban design. The plaza is disconnected from the conventional sewer system, using infiltration planters and subsurface gravel trenches with filter media to reduce hydraulic load. It incorporates indented surface zones designed as temporary flood zones and recharges groundwater rather than draining rainwater to the sewer.
physical_innovation: The design establishes a plaza that performs as a multifunctional, water-resilient platform. Rainwater is managed on-site via permeable pavers, infiltration planters, gravel trenches and dedicated flood-zones – eliminating direct connection to the sewer and recharging groundwater. The use of recycled hardscape material from the old railyard emphasises resource reuse and harmonises with the historic industrial context.
social_innovation: The transformation turns a former industrial yard into a public square that supports everyday use, social gathering and environmental awareness. By embedding visible water-management infrastructure (planters, flood zones) into a comfortable urban plaza with shade trees (e.g., cherry trees) and seating, the project fosters a public realm that educates, activates and connects citizens with site-specific ecological processes.
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.
c5_impacts:
Visible water-sensitive design as public awareness tool
By integrating infiltration planters, permeable surfaces and designated flood zones directly into the plaza’s layout, the project makes water management processes visible to all users. This strengthens public awareness of climate adaptation and turns the square into a daily learning environment where hydrological cycles become tangible.
Circular use of materials from the former railyard
The reuse of hardscape materials salvaged from the old industrial site demonstrates a concrete application of circular economy principles. The continuity in textures and materials preserves the site’s memory while reducing the environmental footprint traditionally associated with plaza construction.
Activation of a former industrial void as a social space
The transformation of an abandoned railyard surface into a multifunctional plaza generates new opportunities for gathering, leisure and open-air activities. Shaded seating, cherry trees and accessible pathways encourage everyday use, supporting community life and soft mobility within the district.

title: Brantstraße – Animal-Aided Design
designer: Landscape architect Thomas E. Hauck & ecologist Wolfgang Weisser (AAD method)
promoter: Bavarian State Ministry for the Environment and Consumer Protection; Munich Housing D.nt
description: The Brantstraße project in Munich is the world’s first built example of Animal-Aided Design (AAD). It integrates habitat features for selected target species into the design of residential outdoor spaces. Nesting structures, feeding habitats, micro-wetlands, flowering meadows and species-specific landscape elements were implemented to enable coexistence between humans and urban fauna. The project transforms an ordinary housing area into a biodiversity-supporting environment embedded within daily life.
physical_innovation: Integration of species-specific micro-habitats into residential outdoor spaces, including nesting boxes, structured vegetation layers, continuous flowering meadows and micro-water elements. The design ensures essential life-cycle requirements (breeding, feeding, shelter) for target species directly within the built environment.
social_innovation: The project raises ecological awareness among residents by embedding fauna-supportive features in everyday spaces. Educational signage and community involvement help residents understand how their environment coexists with birds, insects and hedgehogs, strengthening environmental stewardship.
digital_innovation: Digital ecological tools and AAD planning software were used to map life-cycle needs of animals, matching each need with a corresponding landscape or architectural intervention.
c5_impacts:
Biodiversity integrated into everyday living
By embedding nesting boxes, flowering meadows and feeding habitats into the housing courtyard, the project enables residents to live daily alongside birds, insects and small mammals. This fosters ecological awareness and makes biodiversity a tangible part of neighbourhood life.
Life-cycle habitats designed for target species
Animal-Aided Design identifies the full life-cycle needs of selected species and translates them into concrete spatial interventions. Brantstraße demonstrates how urban development can provide breeding, shelter and feeding habitats within a residential setting.
Educational value for residents and planners
Interpretive elements and the visibility of habitat structures help residents understand ecological processes. The project also serves as a reference model for urban planners, showing how fauna-oriented design can be integrated into regulatory planning and housing development.

title: Kettingplein
description: The Kettingplein project transforms an under-used small square in the heart of a residential neighbourhood in Ghent into a “climate square” with green raingarden features, removal of car-traffic, and redesigned surfaces. Rainwater from adjacent roads and roofs is directed into the new square, stored and infiltrated (approx. 100 m³ capacity) via bowl-shaped raingarden basins and underground storage. The space is designed as a car-free, shaded, green room for the neighbourhood.
physical_innovation: The intervention reduces hard paved surfaces significantly, replaces them with green spaces and gentle depressions to create a raingarden that stores and infiltrates storm-water up to approx. 100 m³. The square is freed from cars and designed as a shared pedestrian/cyclist zone with seating, shade trees and organic forms
social_innovation: The redesign supports neighbourhood life by creating a comfortable and accessible public space where residents can meet and linger. A participatory process included local residents to shape the design, thereby reinforcing ownership and using the space as a “living room” for the communit
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.
c5_impacts:
Local infiltration and water buffering capacity
The redesigned square handles a total storage volume of around 100 m³ of rainwater from adjacent roads and roofs, channelled into depressions and underground storage, significantly reducing surface runoff and improving local storm resilience. 
Improved neighbourhood comfort and greenery
By replacing large areas of impermeable paving with green planting beds, shade trees and a calm pedestrian-friendly layout, the project creates a comfortable “living room” in the neighbourhood, supporting social use, outdoor activities and slower mobility.
Enhanced community involvement and engagement
The design process included participatory workshops with around 50 local residents in 2017, allowing their input on features such as slope gradients, seating design and access for older users and those with limited mobility, strengthening local ownership of the public space.

title: Ciudad Dulce
designer: Municipality of Curridabat + interdisciplinary team (ecologists, urban designers)
description: Ciudad Dulce is a city-wide ecological and social regeneration programme that reconceives Curridabat as a multispecies city. Through pollinator corridors, neighbourhood gardens, permeable streets, composting systems and urban food production, it embeds biodiversity into everyday life. The project reframes nature as civic infrastructure and recognises non-human species as urban inhabitants, reshaping the environmental and social fabric of the city.
physical_innovation: The programme delivers a distributed system of ecological micro-interventions—pollinator gardens, tree-lined corridors, micro-wetlands, permeable sidewalks and community orchards—integrated directly into residential streets, schools and public spaces. This granular strategy improves shade, soil permeability, microclimate and habitat diversity throughout the urban fabric.
social_innovation: Ciudad Dulce pioneers a multispecies citizenship model by recognising pollinators and urban fauna as members of the community. Social innovation emerges through shared gardening, community composting, ecological education, neighbourhood stewardship networks and tools that promote collective care. These practices strengthen social cohesion, environmental awareness and everyday participation.
digital_innovation: Digital transformation is anchored in the “Yo Alcalde” civic platform, which allows residents to report environmental issues, map local needs and collaborate on habitat maintenance. This tool facilitates transparent communication between citizens and administration, enhances participatory governance and supports the monitoring of green infrastructure across neighbourhoods.
c5_impacts:
Biodiversity integrated into daily urban life
Pollinator gardens, ecological corridors and micro-habitats are embedded in neighbourhood streets and parks, making biodiversity visible and tangible. This strengthens ecological resilience and expands everyday contact with nature.
Community empowerment through ecological stewardship
Residents engage in composting, community gardening and shared maintenance activities, generating a sense of collective care and reinforcing social cohesion around environmental practices.
Enhanced environmental health through diffuse green infrastructure
The widespread introduction of vegetation, permeable surfaces and shade trees improves urban microclimate, reduces heat stress and enhances the overall quality of public spaces in a tropical context.

title: Grätzloasen – Neighbourhood Oases
designer: Lokale Agenda 21 Wien + participating citizen groups
promoter: City of Vienna + Lokale Agenda 21 Wien
description: Grätzloasen are small-scale green installations and parklets created by residents, neighbourhood groups and associations in collaboration with the City of Vienna. By converting parking spaces, street edges and residual areas into micro-parks with planting, benches and shading elements, the programme promotes social interaction, local identity, urban greening and heat mitigation. It is a bottom-up system enabling citizens to design, build and maintain small public spaces that improve liveability in dense neighbourhoods.
physical_innovation: The project transforms parking bays, sidewalks and small paved areas into temporary green micro-spaces equipped with planters, mobile seating, permeable surfaces and shading structures. These lightweight, modular installations reduce sealed surfaces, introduce vegetation and provide immediate improvements in comfort and walkability.
social_innovation: Grätzloasen are co-designed and co-built by residents through participatory workshops and community proposals. This model empowers neighbourhood groups, strengthens local ties, promotes collective care practices and fosters active engagement with public space. The programme provides funding, mentoring and tools to support citizen-led placemaking.
digital_innovation: The programme uses online platforms for open calls, application procedures, mapping existing parklets and sharing design guidelines. Digital tools help coordinate community groups, document processes and disseminate replicable solutions for small-scale urban greening.
c5_impacts:
Community ownership of public space
Grätzloasen strengthen social cohesion by enabling residents to collectively design, build and care for small public oases. This creates a sense of shared responsibility and enhances neighbourhood identity.
Micro-green spaces that improve liveability
By adding vegetation, shade and permeable surfaces, parklets improve comfort in highly paved areas, reduce heat accumulation and provide everyday opportunities for rest and informal social interaction.
Low-cost, scalable transformation of streets
The programme demonstrates that small, modular interventions can quickly convert parking spaces into people-centred areas, promoting walkability and preparing neighbourhoods for broader climate adaptation measures.

title: Orto WOW
designer: OrtiAlti landscape architects and social innovation team
promoter: City of Turin and local associations (within ProGiReg / EU Horizon 2020)
description: Orto WOW transforms a former industrial complex in Mirafiori Sud, Turin, into a productive green infrastructure combining a rooftop garden, a pollinator-friendly garden, an apiary and community spaces. The project enhances biodiversity, supports urban food production, and introduces nature as a driver of social inclusion, environmental education and neighbourhood regeneration. Orto WOW is part of the EU project ProGiReg and integrates ecological restoration with community-based management.
physical_innovation: The intervention includes a rooftop garden, raised wooden beds, pollinator-friendly planting, a small apiary, permeable surfaces and micro-habitat structures. These elements reactivate a formerly sealed industrial site, increase biodiversity, create ecological corridors and provide new outdoor spaces for community use.
social_innovation: Orto WOW enables shared governance through a collaboration pact among associations, citizens, cooperatives and municipal actors. Activities include environmental education, collective gardening, workshops, volunteering, social agriculture and inclusion initiatives, reinforcing community cohesion and shared care of the space.
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.
c5_impacts:
Ecological regeneration of a post-industrial site
The creation of a rooftop garden, pollinator beds and an apiary reintroduces biodiversity into a formerly sealed industrial area, enhancing ecological connectivity and providing habitat for pollinators.
Strengthened community cohesion through shared stewardship
Workshops, collective gardening and social agriculture activities foster collaboration between associations, residents, schools and volunteers, increasing community ownership and social inclusion.
Educational impact on urban biodiversity and food production
The garden and apiary serve as open-air classrooms, enabling children, families and citizens to learn about pollinators, soil health, urban agriculture and sustainable practices.

title: Parque Bicentenario
description: Parque Bicentenario is a major urban regeneration project that reconnects two areas of Bogotá long divided by the construction of Avenida El Dorado. Built as a large elevated park spanning over a transport corridor, it integrates terraces, ramps, plazas and green spaces to restore pedestrian continuity and expand public life. The project physically “stitches” an urban wound by recreating links to the historic Parque de la Independencia while offering new areas for leisure, culture, mobility and ecological restoration.
physical_innovation: The park creates a continuous elevated landscape above an existing road trench, combining structural decking, terraced platforms, vegetated slopes, plazas, and pedestrian ramps. It reintroduces green areas over a highly artificial setting and reconnects broken urban edges through walkable infrastructure, integrating vegetation and rest areas into a complex multi-level design.
social_innovation: By bridging neighbourhoods once physically divided, the project improves accessibility to cultural institutions and creates new inclusive public spaces for walking, gathering, leisure and informal activities. The restoration of continuity to Parque de la Independencia revives historical memory and strengthens social attachment to the area, fostering renewed urban identity.
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.
c5_impacts:
Reconnection of fragmented urban fabric
By bridging a major road corridor, the park restores pedestrian continuity between formerly disconnected districts, significantly improving accessibility to cultural and civic spaces.
Transformation of a traffic barrier into public space
The elevated deck turns a previously hostile road trench into a multifunctional urban park, increasing walkability, comfort and opportunities for public use in a densely built area.
Revitalization of historical green heritage
The project re-establishes continuity with Parque de la Independencia, reviving a historic landscape interrupted by mid-20th-century infrastructure and enhancing civic memory and identity.

title: Linear Park Ferrocarril de Cuernavaca
description: The Linear Park Ferrocarril de Cuernavaca transforms a former railway corridor into a continuous urban greenway, reconnecting neighbourhoods across Mexico City through a 4.5 km landscape strategy. The built first phase (1.4 km) integrates forest-like planting, pedestrian and cycling paths, plazas, sports areas and ecological corridors. It restores public space in dense urban areas, promotes active mobility, and creates a linear urban forest that links 22 neighbourhoods.
physical_innovation: The project converts a disused railway into a multifunctional green corridor with dense tree planting, permeable paths, sports areas, rest zones and ecological micro-habitats. It creates a linear urban forest, integrating nature with mobility, recreation and neighbourhood reconnection.
social_innovation: The park provides safe, inclusive and accessible public space in areas lacking recreational infrastructure. It encourages walking and cycling, supports everyday social life and fosters a shared sense of identity along neighbourhoods historically separated by the railway infrastructure.
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.
c5_impacts:
Green reactivation of a disused railway corridor
Transforming an abandoned rail line into a linear urban forest improves ecological connectivity and introduces new habitat for biodiversity in a densely urbanised context.
Enhanced pedestrian and cycling mobility
The new pathway system creates a safe, continuous and shaded mobility corridor, encouraging walking and cycling while linking 22 neighbourhoods previously disconnected.
Improved urban well-being through accessible public space
New plazas, rest areas and shaded zones offer everyday outdoor opportunities for socialisation, sport and recreation, improving quality of life in areas lacking green infrastructure.

title: Îlots de fraîcheur (Isles of Coolness)
description: The Îlots de fraîcheur programme is a city-wide network of cooling spots designed to help Paris cope with extreme heat. The initiative maps and enhances more than 1,400 public cool areas—including shaded parks, fountains, misting devices, permeable plazas, and naturally cooled public buildings—offering accessible refuges during heatwaves. The system creates distributed thermal comfort infrastructure integrated into urban life and the city's heatwave emergency plan (Plan Canicule).
physical_innovation: The programme introduces a distributed system of cooling infrastructures across Paris, combining vegetation, water, permeable materials and purpose-built micro-architectures. In addition to shaded parks and misting devices, several pilot îlots de fraîcheur incorporate lightweight canopy structures, refrigerated benches, and shaded seating modules equipped with evaporative cooling or integrated airflow systems. These micro-architectures create comfortable resting zones even in highly mineral urban areas, extending the cooling effect to streets, squares and schoolyards where natural shade is limited. The combination of vegetated surfaces, permeable pavements, water atomisation and engineered cooling structures forms a hybrid NBS–tech system that reduces local heat accumulation and enhances thermal comfort in dense neighbourhoods.
social_innovation: The programme prioritizes vulnerable groups (derly, children, isolated individuals) by providing a publicly accessible map of cool areas, extended opening hours of public buildings, and community awareness campaigns. The system reshapes heatwave response as a shared civic responsibility.
digital_innovation: A digital interactive map (“Paris – Où se rafraîchir ?”) displays all cooling spots in real time, including opening hours, shade levels, water points and accessibility features. The tool is integrated with the city’s heatwave alert system and mobile applications.
c5_impacts:
City-wide thermal comfort infrastructure
The programme distributes more than 1,400 cooling spots across Paris, offering shaded, vegetated and water-equipped places that significantly reduce heat stress during extreme temperatures.
Improved protection for vulnerable groups
Through targeted communication, extended opening hours of public buildings and easily accessible digital maps, the system supports elderly people, families, children and isolated residents during heatwaves.
Integration of cooling strategies into everyday urban life
By transforming parks, schoolyards and public buildings into cool refuges, Paris embeds climate adaptation into the city’s routine functioning, creating a multi-layered network of comfortable outdoor and indoor spaces.

title: Bankside Urban Forest
designer: Witherford Watson Mann Architects + Better Bankside Urban Design Team
promoter: Better Bankside BID and London Borough of Southwark
description: Bankside Urban Forest is a long-term urban regeneration strategy that reimagines the dense and mineral fabric of the Bankside district as a connected network of green streets, pocket parks, planted squares and pedestrian routes. Rather than creating a single forest, the project implements distributed micro-interventions—tree planting, widened sidewalks, seasonal gardens, vegetated benches and shaded civic spaces—to enhance ecological connectivity, thermal comfort, biodiversity and social life. The strategy is co-developed with local businesses, cultural institutions (such as Tate Modern) and residents.
physical_innovation: Transformation of streets and leftover spaces into a distributed system of green infrastructures: tree-lined routes, permeable surfaces, planted benches, vegetated viaducts, pocket parks and seasonal gardens. Streets are redesigned to prioritise pedestrians and create shaded microclimates, improving walkability and environmental resilience.
social_innovation: The programme is co-created with residents, businesses and cultural organisations. It supports community stewardship, activates underused areas, fosters social cohesion and creates opportunities for participation in urban greening. Public spaces become shared neighbourhood assets shaped by local identity.
digital_innovation: No evidence of embedded digital or smart systems.
c5_impacts:
Distributed greening of a dense urban district
Through micro-interventions—tree planting, pocket parks, planted benches and seasonal vegetation—the project has significantly increased green presence in narrow streets and hardscaped areas, improving comfort and urban character.
Improved pedestrian experience and connectivity
Greener streets and widened sidewalks create safer, more attractive routes linking key landmarks (Tate Modern, Borough Market, riverfront), enhancing walkability and local economic vitality.
Strengthened community involvement and stewardship
Businesses, cultural institutions and residents actively participate in planting, maintenance and design decisions, fostering a sense of shared responsibility and long-term care for public space.

title: Parc des Coteaux
designer: Jean-Pierre Clarac, Laurent Fagart, Claude Allier
promoter: GPV Rive Droite, Cities of Floirac, Cenon, Lormont, Bassens, Carbon-Blanc, Bordeaux Métropole
description: The Parc des Coteaux is a vast network of natural spaces located on the right bank of the Bordeaux metropolis. Developed gradually since the 2000s, it now connects several parks and natural areas spread over the communes of Floirac, Cenon, Lormont, Bassens and Carbon-Blanc. With nearly 500 hectares of woodland, meadows, wetlands and landscaped areas, it is one of the main green infrastructure of the metropolis. The project is based on a logic of ecological continuity and intermunicipal governance, aiming to reconcile the preservation of biodiversity, recreational uses and enhancement of natural and landscape heritage.
physical_innovation: Metropolitan ecological park network connecting multiple existing natural areas through ecological continuity and shared management.
social_innovation: Intermunicipal governance ("Parc LAB") combining biodiversity management, public access and collaborative stewardship.
digital_innovation: None.
c5_impacts: Metropolitan ecological network of 500 hectares connecting multiple municipalities; enhancement of biodiversity through ecological management (late mowing, eco-grazing, habitat restoration, ponds, nesting boxes); improved access to nature and soft mobility; strengthened intermunicipal governance and public awareness of biodiversity.

title: Natur-Park Südgelände
description: It is an old railway site converted into a nature reserve. Located in the middle of Berlin, this project has been an important natural landmark since 1990. After the abandonment of railway sites, the main objective of the project was not to destroy existing structures, but rather to achieve a hybridization between buildings and nature. The site was left in semi-free evolution, with spontaneous vegetation. Railway sites are particularly well suited to keeping industrial traces while allowing a multitude of habitats and natural areas. The park today is home to significant urban biodiversity, industrial heritage, and public uses.
physical_innovation: The project preserves and integrates former railway infrastructure within a naturally evolving ecosystem. Instead of replacing industrial heritage with conventional landscaping, spontaneous vegetation and ecological succession were maintained and enhanced, creating a hybrid landscape where nature and industrial structures coexist.
social_innovation: Natur-Park Südgelände demonstrates how abandoned industrial land can be reappropriated as a public ecological space while preserving local identity and memory. The project successfully combines environmental education, recreation and heritage conservation within an urban biodiversity hotspot.
digital_innovation: None identified.
c5_impacts: Natur-Park Südgelände demonstrates how abandoned railway land can become a biodiversity hotspot within a dense urban environment. The preservation of spontaneous vegetation and industrial structures has created a diverse mosaic of habitats supporting a rich fauna and flora. The project contributes to climate resilience through extensive vegetation cover and low-intervention management. Socially, it enables the public reappropriation of a former industrial wasteland while preserving local heritage and fostering environmental awareness. The coexistence of conservation objectives, industrial memory and recreational uses makes Südgelände an internationally recognised model of urban ecological regeneration.

title: High Line
designer: James Corner, Piet Oudolf, Diller Scofidio + Renfro
promoter: Friends of the High Line, New York City Department of Parks & Recreation
description: The High Line is a former aerial railway located in Manhattan, transformed into a linear park between 2006 and 2014. Originally intended for the transport of goods, the infrastructure was abandoned in the 1980s before being saved thanks to citizen mobilization. The project is based on spontaneous vegetation that had colonized the rails for several decades and seeks to preserve the industrial identity of the site while creating a green public space. Today, the High Line is an emblematic example of the reuse of urban infrastructure for renaturation, combining biodiversity, soft mobility, social uses and heritage enhancement.
physical_innovation: Transformation of an abandoned elevated railway into a linear ecological park integrating urban biodiversity, stormwater management and public space.
social_innovation: Citizen-led preservation and management model through Friends of the High Line, combining public access, cultural programming and environmental education.
c5_impacts: Conversion of an abandoned elevated railway into a multifunctional green corridor. The project increased urban biodiversity, improved stormwater infiltration, enhanced pedestrian connectivity, preserved industrial heritage and created a major public space attracting millions of visitors annually. The project also became a reference case for adaptive reuse and nature-based urban regeneration, while generating debates regarding green gentrification and rising property values in adjacent neighbourhoods.

title: Pla BUITS
description: The Pla Buits programme ("Empty spaces with territorial and social involvement") is an initiative launched by the municipality of Barcelona in 2012 to temporarily reactivate vacant land belonging to the city. In a context of economic crisis and many urban projects at a standstill, the municipality has made unused plots available for associations, collectives and non-profit organizations. These spaces have hosted shared gardens, urban agriculture projects, artistic installations and meeting places. The project is based on the idea of a temporary occupation of wastelands as a tool for renaturation, urban experimentation and citizen participation.
physical_innovation: Temporary activation of vacant municipal plots through reversible community-led uses.
social_innovation: Co-management of public land by local associations and citizens through open calls.
digital_innovation: None
c5_impacts: Temporary regeneration of vacant municipal plots through community-led activities, increasing urban greenery, biodiversity, social cohesion and citizen participation while testing future uses of underutilised land.

title: Tiny Forest (Miyawaki Method)
description: Tiny Forests are small urban plantations inspired by the method developed by the Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki. The principle is to plant many local species in a very dense manner on small areas, in order to accelerate plant growth and quickly recreate an autonomous forest ecosystem. Introduced in Europe from 2015 in the Netherlands, then developed in several cities such as Paris, Lyon, Brussels or London, these micro-forests are today used as tools for urban renaturalization, fight against heat islands and biodiversity awareness.
physical_innovation: Dense planting of native species on small urban plots to rapidly create self-sustaining forest ecosystems.
social_innovation: Citizen participation and environmental education through collective planting and monitoring activities.
digital_innovation: None
c5_impacts: Creation of dense native urban forests on small plots, increasing biodiversity, improving microclimatic conditions, enhancing rainwater infiltration and strengthening citizen engagement through participatory planting and environmental education.

title: Superilles
description: Les Superilles is an urban planning model developed in Barcelona from the 2010s to reduce the role of cars in public spaces. The principle is to group together several urban islands (generally 3 × 3 blocks) where transit traffic is strongly limited within the perimeter. The liberated streets are then redeveloped to accommodate more vegetation, public spaces, games, soft mobility and collective uses. The project aims to improve quality of life, reduce pollution and enhance biodiversity while creating more livable neighborhoods.
physical_innovation: Reallocation of street space from motorised traffic to green infrastructure, public space and active mobility.
social_innovation: Reclaiming public space for residents through participatory urban transformation and multifunctional street uses.
digital_innovation: None
c5_impacts: Transformation of car-dominated streets into multifunctional public spaces with increased greenery, improved air quality, reduced noise, enhanced biodiversity, safer active mobility and stronger social interaction.

title: MARES Madrid
designer: Ayuntamiento de Madrid and project consortium
description: The MARES project (Madrid Recupera, Alimenta, Recicla, Energía y Social) is an urban transformation program developed between 2016 and 2019 in several districts of Madrid. This is a project funded by the European Union (Urban Innovative Actions) which aims to strengthen urban resilience through the social and solidarity economy. The project relies on the reactivation of buildings and public spaces in disrepair to transform them into laboratories for social and economic innovation. It acts on five key sectors (mobility, food, recycling, energy and care) to create local, sustainable and inclusive productive activities.
physical_innovation: Adaptive reuse of vacant buildings and public facilities as hubs for social innovation, circular economy and local resilience.
social_innovation: Creation of neighbourhood laboratories supporting social entrepreneurship, community initiatives and collaborative governance.
digital_innovation: Collaborative innovation platforms and knowledge-sharing networks.
c5_impacts: MARES transformed underused public buildings into neighbourhood innovation hubs supporting social entrepreneurship, circular economy initiatives, sustainable mobility, local food systems and community-based services. The project strengthened urban resilience, social inclusion and local employment through collaborative governance and experimentation.

title: Parc Desjardins
description:
Desjardins Park is located as part of the conversion of the former Desjardins military barracks in Angers. The project is part of an urban renewal operation launched in the early 2000s, aimed at transforming a closed military enclave into a new residential district structured around a large central park. The site now hosts a landscaped area of about 1 to 1.6 hectares integrated into a neighborhood of about 6.6 hectares, designed according to the principle of the "inhabited park", where vegetation structures all urban forms and uses. 
The project is based on a strong approach of consultation with the inhabitants, who have helped to define the uses of the park and its programming. The park is delivered even before the end of the neighborhood in order to support the gradual appropriation of the site.
physical_innovation: Transformation of a former military brownfield into a “park-inhabited” neighbourhood structured around a central multifunctional green space.
social_innovation: Strong citizen participation in the definition of park uses and early delivery of the park to support neighbourhood appropriation.
c5_impacts: The Desjardins Park transformed a former military brownfield into a multifunctional green public space that structures a new residential neighbourhood. Through ecological landscaping, permeable surfaces and participatory planning, the project improved biodiversity, urban liveability and social cohesion while supporting the gradual appropriation of the site by residents.

title: Parque del Agua
description:
The Parque del Agua Luis Buñuel is a large urban park of more than 120 hectares located in the meander of Ranillas, in Zaragoza, along the Ebro river. It was created as part of the 2008 International Exhibition on the theme of water, on a former site of huertas (agricultural gardens). The project transforms this former agricultural area into a large multifunctional park combining biodiversity, water management, recreation and sports infrastructure. It is designed as a "hydraulic" landscape where the water of the river structures uses, habitats and developments. 
The park is also designed as a resilient space against river floods: some areas are deliberately flood prone, which allows to manage the natural overflows of the Ebro while maintaining the ecological functions of the site.
physical_innovation: Large-scale water-oriented urban park integrating flood management, biodiversity, recreation and ecological restoration.
social_innovation: Combination of ecological functions, public recreation and metropolitan accessibility within a resilient landscape framework.
c5_impacts: The Parque del Agua Luis Buñuel transformed former agricultural land into a large metropolitan park combining ecological restoration, flood resilience, biodiversity enhancement and recreational activities. The project uses water as a structuring landscape element while improving urban liveability and climate adaptation capacity.

title: Green Corridors
description:
València’s “Green Coasts” refer to an urban strategy of renaturation and ecological connection on a metropolitan scale, structured around the Jardín del Turia and its potential extensions. The most emblematic case is that of projects to extend and connect the old bed of the Turia river (transformed into an urban park since the 1980s) with other neighborhoods, infrastructure and natural spaces, especially in the south of the city and towards the coastal facade. These corridors are part of a "green infrastructure" network aimed at connecting existing large green spaces, reducing urban fragmentation and strengthening the city’s climate resilience. 
The general idea is to transform old transport routes, railway wastelands or underused urban spaces into plant continuities promoting soft mobility, biodiversity and quality of life.
physical_innovation: Creation of a metropolitan green infrastructure network connecting parks, former infrastructures and urban open spaces through ecological corridors and active mobility routes.
social_innovation: Integration of biodiversity, mobility and public space through large-scale urban regeneration and participatory planning processes.
c5_impacts: The Green Corridors strategy strengthens ecological connectivity across València by linking parks, public spaces and natural areas through a network of vegetated routes. The project improves biodiversity, climate resilience, active mobility and urban liveability while supporting long-term metropolitan green infrastructure planning.

title: Boscoincittà
designer: Italia Nostra, Centro di Forestazione Urbana
description: Boscoincittà is the first example of urban forest in Italy, created in 1974 west of Milan at the initiative of the association Italia Nostra, on abandoned agricultural land made available by the municipality. The project gradually transforms a semi-abandoned area into a large natural park of more than 110 to 120 hectares, consisting of woods, meadows, wetlands, rivers and agricultural areas. Unlike a classic park, it is a “urban fortification” project where nature is deliberately built, but evolving, with a strong dimension of citizen participation and continuous management. The site also includes shared gardens, educational facilities, wetlands and a wide variety of plant species, creating a hybrid landscape between controlled nature and spontaneous ecological dynamics.
physical_innovation: Progressive transformation of degraded agricultural land into a multifunctional urban forest combining woodland, wetlands, meadows and educational spaces.
social_innovation: Long-term co-management involving volunteers, schools, associations and public authorities in the creation and maintenance of the urban forest.
c5_impacts: Boscoincittà transformed degraded agricultural land into one of Europe's earliest urban forestry projects. Through long-term ecological restoration, citizen participation and adaptive management, the project created a diverse mosaic of woodlands, meadows and wetlands that enhances biodiversity, climate resilience and urban liveability.

title: Athens Pocket Parks
designer: Municipality of Athens and partner landscape design teams
description:
The Athens Pocket Parks is a municipal program launched from 2020–2021 aimed at transforming small abandoned or underused urban plots into micro-green spaces. These interventions are dispersed in several dense neighborhoods (Kypseli, Kolonos, Pagrati, Metaxourgeio, etc.) and are part of the "Adopt your City" strategy, which involves the municipality and private or associative actors to finance and realize these spaces. The goal is to create small-scale “islands of freshness” in a very compact and mineralized city, improving both local biodiversity and the quality of daily life. 
These areas are generally built on former wastelands or vacant lots, with strong attention paid to vegetation, water management and the reintroduction of nature in very dense environments.
physical_innovation: Conversion of vacant urban plots into small green public spaces providing cooling, biodiversity and local ecosystem services.
social_innovation: Public-private partnerships supporting neighbourhood-scale urban greening and regeneration.
c5_impacts: The Athens Pocket Parks programme converts vacant urban plots into small green public spaces that improve biodiversity, urban cooling and neighbourhood liveability. Through public-private partnerships, the initiative creates a distributed network of local green infrastructure across dense urban districts.

title: Réseau des jardins sauvages
designer: Nantes Métropole, Ville de Nantes, Écopôle / CPIE Pays de Nantes & local associations
description:
In Nantes, there is the "wild gardens network", a widespread municipal and associative strategy for developing biodiversity in the city. This brings together several complementary measures: differentiated management of green spaces, preservation of spontaneous flora, ecological collective gardens, gardened streets, and actions led by associative networks such as Écopôle / CPIE Pays de Nantes. The whole aims to leave more room for spontaneous vegetation and to consider certain urban spaces as ecological habitats in their own right. 
In this logic, the city is not limited to creating parks, but seeks to build a distributed green grid, composed of micro-spaces, shared gardens, environmentally maintained wastelands and citizen interventions in public space.
physical_innovation: Distributed ecological management strategy integrating spontaneous vegetation, community gardens, ecological corridors and citizen-led greening interventions.
social_innovation: Co-production of urban biodiversity through collaboration between public authorities, associations and residents.
c5_impacts: The Nantes wild gardens and spontaneous biodiversity network demonstrates how a distributed system of community gardens, ecological management practices and citizen-led greening initiatives can strengthen urban biodiversity, ecological connectivity and social cohesion. By recognising spontaneous vegetation as a resource rather than a constraint, the strategy promotes a resilient and ecosystem-based approach to urban planning.

title: Gardens by the Bay
description: Gardens by the Bay is a 101-hectare urban park developed on reclaimed land in Singapore's Marina Bay district and inaugurated in 2012. As one of the flagship projects of Singapore's "City in a Garden" strategy, it integrates landscape architecture, ecological engineering and environmental technologies to create a multifunctional green infrastructure. Combining themed gardens, climate-controlled conservatories, the iconic Supertrees and extensive public spaces, the project demonstrates how biodiversity, climate adaptation, education and tourism can be successfully integrated within a dense metropolitan environment.
physical_innovation: Transformation of reclaimed land into a multifunctional ecological park integrating themed gardens, climate-controlled conservatories, Supertrees, ecological water management and extensive public landscapes.
social_innovation: Creation of a world-class public park combining recreation, environmental education, tourism and biodiversity conservation while reinforcing Singapore's "City in a Garden" vision.
digital_innovation: Integration of smart environmental technologies including photovoltaic Supertrees, automated environmental monitoring, rainwater harvesting systems and high-efficiency climate control for the conservatories.
c5_impacts: Gardens by the Bay has transformed over 100 hectares of reclaimed land into one of the world's most advanced examples of multifunctional green infrastructure. The project enhances biodiversity, improves urban microclimate, supports rainwater harvesting and renewable energy production, and demonstrates how ecological engineering can be integrated with architecture and public space. Beyond its environmental benefits, the park has become a global reference for sustainable urban development, environmental education and nature-based climate adaptation.

title: Parc Saint-Jean
description: Parc Saint-Jean is a 2.5-hectare urban park inaugurated in 2025 as the central green space of the Saint-Jean district regeneration project in Clermont-Ferrand. Developed on the site of former municipal slaughterhouses, the park is distinguished by its ecological approach, which preserves and enhances the spontaneous vegetation and existing topography rather than replacing them. Combining areas of natural succession, landscaped gardens and public amenities, the project demonstrates how brownfield regeneration can rely on existing ecological dynamics to create a resilient, biodiverse and accessible urban park.
physical_innovation: Transformation of a former industrial brownfield into an urban park by preserving spontaneous woodland, existing landforms and natural ecological processes while introducing complementary public spaces and gardens.
social_innovation: Creation of a neighbourhood park where biodiversity conservation, recreation and local heritage are integrated through immersive pathways, cultural spaces and ecological management.
c5_impacts: The project regenerates a former industrial site into a multifunctional urban park where existing spontaneous vegetation forms the basis of the landscape design. More than 400 trees and thousands of shrubs and perennial plants reinforce ecological continuity, while protected natural areas, immersive boardwalks, gardens and public facilities create a resilient park that supports biodiversity, recreation and neighbourhood renewal.

title: Grønningen-Bispeparken
description: Grønningen-Bispeparken is a 20,000 m² climate park completed in 2024 in Copenhagen's Nordvest district. Designed by SLA Landscape Architects, the project transforms the open spaces of a 1950s social housing estate into a multifunctional green infrastructure where biodiversity, stormwater management and public life are closely integrated. Built around the principle "form follows nature", the park demonstrates how nature-based solutions can simultaneously improve climate resilience, ecological quality and everyday urban life.
physical_innovation: Transformation of underused residential green spaces into a multifunctional climate park where bioswales, native planting and public amenities work together to manage stormwater while enhancing biodiversity.
social_innovation: Integration of climate adaptation into everyday neighbourhood life through participatory design, multifunctional public spaces and landscape features that combine ecological and social functions.
c5_impacts: The project transforms underused residential open spaces into a climate-adaptive park capable of storing and infiltrating more than 3,000 m³ of stormwater through 18 vegetated bioswales. The conservation of mature trees, the planting of 149 new trees from 23 native species and the establishment of diverse habitats improve biodiversity while creating attractive spaces for recreation, community events and everyday neighbourhood life.

title: Hyatt Place Rouen
designer: Espace Libre Paysagistes ; d + b Interior Design
description: Hyatt Place Rouen is a heritage redevelopment project completed in 2024 in Rouen, France. The project transforms the former 19th-century École normale d'institutrices into a mixed-use complex combining a hotel, restaurant, meeting facilities and landscaped outdoor spaces. Rather than a renaturation project, it illustrates how landscape design can enhance heritage rehabilitation by improving environmental quality, visitor experience and urban attractiveness while preserving the site's historical identity.
physical_innovation: Adaptive reuse of a historic institutional site integrating landscape design, heritage conservation and contemporary hospitality functions while preserving existing gardens and mature trees.
social_innovation: Opening a formerly inaccessible heritage site to the public through hospitality, leisure and landscaped outdoor spaces.
c5_impacts: The project demonstrates how landscape design can support the adaptive reuse of a historic building by preserving mature vegetation, improving outdoor comfort and reinforcing the site's heritage value. Gardens, terraces and planted spaces enhance the visitor experience while contributing modestly to urban biodiversity and local microclimate within a dense urban environment.

title: Sjödalsparken
description: Sjödalsparken is a 4-hectare urban park redeveloped between 2018 and 2021 in the centre of Huddinge, south of Stockholm. Designed by LAND arkitektur, the project transforms an underused municipal park into a multifunctional blue-green infrastructure by daylighting the historic Fullerstaån stream and integrating stormwater management, biodiversity, recreation and cultural activities. The park demonstrates how water can become the organising element of urban regeneration while strengthening ecological functions and public life.
physical_innovation: Transformation of an existing urban park into a multifunctional blue-green infrastructure through the daylighting of a buried stream and the integration of ecological water management with public space.
social_innovation: Creation of a central civic park combining ecological restoration, everyday recreation and cultural events around a visible water landscape.
c5_impacts: The project restores the historic Fullerstaån stream as the ecological backbone of the park through open channels, ponds and wetlands that improve stormwater management and create diverse aquatic habitats. Combined with meadows, shrubs and tree planting, the redesigned landscape enhances biodiversity, strengthens the local microclimate and provides a vibrant public space supporting daily recreation as well as festivals, markets and community events.

title: Plaza Enric Granados
description: Plaza Enric Granados – Jardí Illa is a public space redevelopment completed between 2022 and 2023 in Barcelona's Eixample district. Designed by LANDLAB Laboratorio de Paisajes as part of the Superilles (Superblocks) programme, the project transforms a former traffic intersection into a neighbourhood garden that combines climate adaptation, biodiversity, sustainable mobility and social uses. It forms part of Barcelona's wider strategy to create a continuous green network across one of Europe's densest urban districts.
physical_innovation: Transformation of a road intersection into a climate-adaptive neighbourhood garden through depaving, sustainable drainage systems and extensive planting integrated within Barcelona's Superblocks network.
social_innovation: Reallocation of street space from cars to pedestrians, creating a multifunctional public space that strengthens neighbourhood life while improving environmental quality.
c5_impacts: The project replaces a highly impervious traffic junction with a green public square integrating permeable soils, Mediterranean planting and sustainable urban drainage systems (SuDS). By reducing vehicular traffic and increasing tree canopy, it improves stormwater infiltration, urban biodiversity, thermal comfort and air quality while creating a new neighbourhood gathering space connected to Barcelona's wider Superblocks green corridor.

title: Mapletree Business City II
description: Mapletree Business City II is a large mixed-use business park completed in 2016 in Singapore's Pasir Panjang district. Designed by Shma Company Limited in collaboration with DCA Architects, the project redevelops a former industrial logistics site into a biophilic workplace where tropical landscape, stormwater management and employee well-being are integrated into the daily functioning of the campus. It illustrates how nature-based solutions can be applied to large-scale commercial developments.
physical_innovation: Transformation of a former industrial logistics site into a biophilic business park where tropical landscape, bioswales and artificial landforms function as ecological infrastructure while supporting everyday workplace activities.
social_innovation: Development of a workplace environment where landscape becomes a shared social space promoting well-being, outdoor work, recreation and interaction between employees.
c5_impacts: The redevelopment converts a fully sealed industrial site into a lush tropical workplace landscape featuring multilayered vegetation, bioswales and rainwater harvesting systems. The project improves stormwater management, strengthens ecological connectivity with nearby Kent Ridge Park, enhances urban biodiversity and creates comfortable outdoor environments that promote employee well-being, recreation and informal social interaction.

title: Highnote
description: Highnote is a mixed-use residential and public space development completed in 2023 in the city centre of Almere, Netherlands. Designed by Studioninedots with landscape architecture by Flux landscape architecture, the project transforms a former triangular parking lot into a dense urban living environment combining a residential tower and an active public base. It demonstrates how contemporary European cities can convert underused mineral surfaces into layered landscapes integrating housing, public space, and ecological functions.
physical_innovation: Transformation of a highly sealed urban parking area into a vertically and horizontally integrated mixed-use landscape system (“plinth landscape”), where courtyards, terraces, rooftop gardens and semi-public “urban rooms” create a continuous ecological and social gradient between city, housing and nature.
social_innovation: Creation of a hybrid living environment where public, semi-public and private spaces are gradually blended through landscape design (“stadskamers”), allowing continuous social interaction between residents, workers and visitors within a porous urban base.
c5_impacts: The redevelopment transforms a sealed triangular parking lot into a layered mixed-use ecosystem combining housing, public life and landscape infrastructure. Through a system of courtyards, gardens and rooftop landscapes, the project increases urban permeability, introduces stormwater management through vegetated retention areas (wadi systems), and improves microclimatic comfort through shading and evapotranspiration. It strengthens biodiversity in a dense urban centre while creating a continuous social landscape where work, living and public life are interwoven across different spatial thresholds.

title: Suan San Pocket Park
description: Suan San Pocket Park is a small-scale urban regeneration project completed in 2025 in the Khlong San district of Bangkok, Thailand. Designed by Shma Company Limited, it transforms a former abandoned industrial and port-related site along the Chao Phraya River into a neighbourhood pocket park. The project is part of Bangkok’s “15-Minute Parks” strategy, aiming to ensure equitable access to green space within walking distance for residents, while reconnecting fragmented urban areas to the river landscape.
physical_innovation: Transformation of a degraded riverside industrial site into a multifunctional pocket park that reconnects urban fabric and river ecology through landscape design, while preserving existing mature trees and integrating ecological restoration within a dense urban environment.
social_innovation: Development of a participatory neighbourhood park based on co-design with local communities, providing equitable access to green space within a 15-minute walking radius and reinforcing social cohesion in a previously underused and marginalised urban area.
c5_impacts: The project converts a neglected industrial riverside site into a multifunctional neighbourhood pocket park that improves local access to green space and strengthens the ecological continuity along the Chao Phraya River. By preserving mature trees and introducing dense vegetation, it enhances microclimatic comfort and urban biodiversity while reconnecting surrounding neighbourhoods to the waterfront. The park acts as a social infrastructure node, supporting everyday recreational activities, community events and environmental awareness in line with Bangkok’s 15-Minute Park strategy.

title: Chilton Square (Playground)
description: Chilton Square is a public space and playscape project completed between 2023 and 2025 in the King’s Cross redevelopment area in London. Designed by Root And Erect as part of the broader King’s Cross masterplan, it transforms a technically constrained residual site above underground infrastructure into a dense woodland-inspired urban playscape. The project integrates landscape, play, and circulation into a continuous forest-like environment within one of London’s most intensively redeveloped districts.
physical_innovation: Transformation of a technically constrained urban residual space (above underground infrastructure and tunnels) into a multifunctional woodland playscape where forest landscape, play structures and pedestrian circulation are integrated into a single ecological and spatial system.
social_innovation: Creation of a fully open, non-enclosed urban playscape designed as an intergenerational space where children, families and adults share a continuous landscape experience combining play, rest, and pedestrian movement within a dense urban regeneration district.
c5_impacts: The project transforms a highly constrained residual urban site into a dense woodland-inspired public playscape that strengthens the continuity of King’s Cross public realm network. By integrating vegetation, play structures and circulation paths, it enhances microclimatic comfort, increases urban biodiversity, and provides a multifunctional open space embedded within a high-density regeneration district. The co-design process with children contributes to a socially inclusive environment, reinforcing the role of landscape as both ecological infrastructure and everyday urban experience.

title: Parc du Duc de Dino
description: Parc du Duc de Dino is a landscape restoration and enhancement project located in France along the Seine valley. Designed by Bassinet Turquin Paysage, the project concerns a historic aristocratic estate whose park evolved between the 18th and 19th centuries into an English-style landscape garden. The contemporary intervention aims to restore and reveal the historical layers of the site while increasing its accessibility and integrating it into a broader ecological corridor at the territorial scale.
physical_innovation: Restoration and adaptive management of a historic landscape park where ecological processes are reactivated within a cultural heritage framework, integrating biodiversity enhancement with the reading of historical landscape layers (18th–19th century garden structures).
social_innovation: Opening and reactivation of a former aristocratic estate as a public landscape, allowing access to a cultural and scenic heritage site while supporting recreational and educational uses within a managed historic environment.
c5_impacts: The project enhances a historic aristocratic landscape by maintaining and managing its layered heritage structure while increasing ecological connectivity at the territorial scale of the Seine valley. It strengthens biodiversity through differentiated landscape management (woodland edges, clearings, mature tree preservation) and repositions the estate as a cultural and ecological asset accessible for public enjoyment. Rather than restoring a “pristine nature”, the project establishes a living cultural landscape where historical identity, ecological processes and contemporary uses coexist.

title: Jin Wellbeing County
description: Jin Wellbeing County is a large mixed-use development completed in 2020 in Pathum Thani, on the outskirts of Bangkok. Designed by Shma Company Limited, the project is the first senior-oriented residential and healthcare community in Thailand. It transforms a flood-prone peri-urban site into a forest-based living environment where housing, healthcare, public space and ecological systems are fully integrated. The project explores how landscape can function as a therapeutic infrastructure supporting ageing, wellbeing and social cohesion.
physical_innovation: Transformation of a flood-prone peri-urban site into a “forest-based community” where hydrological systems, multi-strata vegetation and healthcare-oriented spatial planning are integrated into a single therapeutic landscape.
social_innovation: Creation of a senior-oriented mixed-use community where landscape becomes an active support system for health, ageing, social interaction and daily life, structured through “Retreat, Engage, Create” spatial dynamics.

title: Tøyen Rainforest
description: Tøyen Rainforest (Regnskog på Tøyen) is a temporary landscape installation completed in 2022 on Tøyen Torg in Oslo. Designed by Grindaker Landskapsarkitekter in collaboration with the City of Oslo and local agencies, the project experiments with rapid and reversible urban greening strategies. It transforms a highly paved public square into a temporary urban forest composed of clustered tree islands, aiming to test how dense vegetation can change microclimate, biodiversity and public use in a highly urbanized context.
physical_innovation: Transformation of a highly paved urban square into a temporary experimental urban rainforest using clustered tree islands and multi-layered vegetation to test rapid reforestation strategies in dense city conditions.
social_innovation: Creation of a temporary immersive forest environment in a central public square, designed as a participatory and educational tool to raise awareness about climate adaptation, biodiversity loss and the potential of rapid urban greening.
c5_impacts: The project demonstrates how a highly paved urban square can be temporarily transformed into a dense forest-like environment using lightweight and reversible interventions. It improves microclimatic conditions locally, increases short-term biodiversity through layered planting, and serves as a public experiment in climate adaptation. The installation also functions as a pedagogical tool, helping citizens understand the effects of urban greening while testing future scenarios for permanent transformation.

title: Liberation Museum of Manisa
description: The Liberation Museum of Manisa is a semi-buried memorial museum completed in 2025 in Manisa, Turkey. Designed by Yalin Architectural Design, the project transforms a 3,800 m² historical site into a landscape-museum where architecture and topography are inseparable. The building is covered by a public park, creating a dual condition: an everyday green space above and a narrative underground museum below, structured as a spatial journey through the historical events of 1918–1923.
physical_innovation: Transformation of a historical site into a semi-buried landscape-museum where architecture is shaped as topography, combining a public park on the surface with an underground narrative spatial sequence structured through earth-covered volumes.
social_innovation: Creation of a public park above a memorial museum, allowing daily public use of the site while simultaneously transmitting collective memory through an immersive spatial journey structured around historical sequences of occupation, destruction, liberation and reconstruction.
c5_impacts: The project integrates a memorial museum into a landscape structure where a public park covers a semi-buried architectural system. It creates a dual-use site combining everyday public space with a narrative underground museum experience. The intervention enhances vegetation cover, reduces heat island effects through earth and green roofing, and transforms historical memory into a spatial and bodily experience. It strengthens public access to a culturally significant site while embedding ecological and climatic benefits into the architectural mass.
